newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE official discusses Iraq with U.N.'s Ekeus.
newsitem.headline: UAE official discusses Iraq with U.N.'s Ekeus.

text.p: A United Arab Emirates cabinet minister on Wednesday discussed Iraq with the United Nations official in charge of eliminating Baghdad's mass destruction weapons, the official news agency WAM said.

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Hamdan bin Zaid al-Nahayan and Rolf Ekeus discussed "recent developments in the Gulf and Iraq's commitment to implementing United Nations (Gulf War) resolutions," it added.
Ekeus, on a regional tour to seek financial support for his comission ahead of a Gulf Arab summit next month, has already been to Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
He arrived in the UAE capital of Abu Dhabi a day after local newspapers launched an unusual attack on him, accusing him of serving "masters" in Washington.
Analysts said the media comments reflected the official position of the UAE, which has made the strongest push for Arab reconciliation with Gulf War foe Iraq.
Officials said on Wednesday Abu Dhabi was urging regional allies to normalise ties with Baghdad.

But differences appear to have sharpened between the UAE and Kuwait, which has rejected such calls and is still bitter over Iraq's lightning invasion in 1990 that shocked militarily vulnerable Gulf Arab states.
Baghdad on Monday accepted U.N. terms to implement a deal signed in May allowing it to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to pay for food and medicine. The deal has yet to be put into effect.
